2
The first night

The first night

Bring Opal home in the afternoon if you can, so she has a few hours to sniff around before bedtime.

Set the crate beside your bed. She can hear you breathe and settles faster.

  • An old towel that smells of her littermates
  • A chew toy sized for small breeds
  • One trip out around 2 am

She may cry for ten minutes or so. A hand on the crate helps more than taking her out.

3
Crate and potty training

Crate and potty training

Bostons learn fast and love a routine. Take her out after every meal, every nap and every play session.

4
Crate and potty training

Praise her the moment she goes, outside, every time. Accidents inside get cleaned with an enzyme cleaner and no fuss.

  • Out first thing in the morning
  • Out within 15 minutes of eating
  • Out last thing at night
5
Feeding

Feeding

Keep Opal on the food she eats here for at least two weeks. If you change, mix it in slowly over 7 to 10 days.

⅓ cup, three times a day, soaked in warm water the first week.

Puppy food program

Some links here are referral or affiliate links: we may earn a commission or credit when you use them, at no cost to you.

6
Boston basics

Boston basics

Bostons are sturdy, funny and very attached to their people. They snore, they love a lap, and they don't love heat: keep walks short on hot days.

Their eyes are large and easy to scratch. Check them daily and call your vet about any redness or squinting.

7

Happy puppy days!
